notes: Identity independently checked in supplied canonical text: title Time, money, and happiness: Does putting a price on time affect our ability to smell the roses?; authors Scott Connors, Mansur Khamitov, Sarah Moroz, Lorne Campbell, Claire Henderson; Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 67 (2016) 60–64; DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2015.08.005. This is the full primary replication report (title/abstract, Methods, Results, Tables 1–2, Discussion, References), not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF was supplied; no render performed. Target mapping uses Table 2 title (impatience), the explicitly named Replication 1 row, and the η2p column under Interaction effect; no effect-size conversion. The source prints partial eta-squared, retained despite requested etasq. Same-test printed p = .046, exact, and F = 4.01, denominator df = 262, retained in es.test_statistic; p_r is not assigned. N is directly printed, not calculated or inferred from df. First replication: eight participants excluded for technical problems listening to the music; three removed for prior participation in a similar study. N = 266 is explicitly final and is also printed in the target ANOVA table. Original side and p_r are unassigned placeholders. The significant interaction was described as contrary to the original pattern, supporting the authors’ failed verdict rather than a significance-based success inference.
